strings.name: Ma Ying-jeou
strings.role: Former president of Taiwan; Kuomintang politician
strings.summary: Ma Ying-jeou entered elected politics after legal and administrative work, serving as Taipei mayor and president from 2008 to 2016. He promoted cross-strait economic exchanges and met Xi Jinping. These policies also sparked debates over democratic oversight, economic dependence and Taiwan’s future. After office, he continued participating in public discussion of cross-strait relations.
strings.coverageNote: Reviewed through 18 November 2026; the latest verified personal meeting was on 9 July. Elections and accession, agreement signature and entry into force, meetings during and after office, and separate legal proceedings are distinguished.
strings.influence.rationale: Formerly led Taiwan and participated in cross-strait exchanges and related policy, influencing discussion of regional relations.
strings.facts.f1.label: Birth and legal education
strings.facts.f1.value: Born in Hong Kong on 13 July 1950. He graduated in law from National Taiwan University in 1972, earned an NYU LL.M. in 1976 and a Harvard Law School S.J.D. in 1981. The latter is a Doctor of Juridical Science degree.
strings.facts.f2.label: Early public offices
strings.facts.f2.value: He joined the Presidential Office in 1981 and served as Chiang Ching-kuo’s English secretary. He chaired the Research, Development and Evaluation Commission from 1988, became Mainland Affairs Council deputy minister in 1991 and justice minister in 1993. These administrative posts differed from his later elected offices.
strings.highlights.h1.title: Exchange policy and public oversight
strings.highlights.h1.text: He supported expanded cross-strait trade and personal exchanges. ECFA provided an economic cooperation framework, but scrutiny of the subsequent services agreement sparked protests, highlighting transparency, democratic oversight and political trust alongside economic cooperation.
strings.highlights.h2.title: Separate proceedings require separate treatment
strings.highlights.h2.text: The Three Media case concerned asset transactions during his KMT leadership and ended in a final acquittal. Reports in 2026 described a separate foundation-finance investigation involving different parties and denials of allegations. The facts and procedural status of the two cases are distinct.
strings.timeline.t1.title: Acquittal becomes final in Three Media case
strings.timeline.t1.text: CNA reported that the Supreme Court dismissed the prosecution’s appeal, making the acquittals of Ma and others final. This was not a decision not to prosecute; convictions of other defendants cannot be attributed to him.
strings.timeline.t2.title: Meets Xi Jinping again in Beijing after leaving office
strings.timeline.t2.text: At the Great Hall of the People, he advocated peaceful cross-strait development. He attended as a former president, unlike the 2015 Singapore meeting when both leaders held office. Political advocacy is not an implemented institutional settlement.
strings.timeline.t3.title: Meets Xi Jinping in Singapore
strings.timeline.t3.text: The talks were the first between serving leaders of the two sides since their separation in 1949. They discussed cross-strait relations; the meeting itself did not resolve the political disputes.
strings.timeline.t4.title: Services-agreement dispute sparks Sunflower Movement
strings.timeline.t4.text: Students and civic groups entered the legislature, protesting the agreement’s review procedure and demanding oversight. Occupation of the chamber lasted until 10 April. The protest targeted the later services agreement, not the wholesale invalidation of ECFA at that time.
strings.timeline.t5.title: Wins presidential reelection
strings.timeline.t5.text: His ticket with running mate Wu Den-yih won 6,891,139 votes, according to the Central Election Commission. His second presidency ended on 20 May 2016; election day and term boundaries are different dates.
strings.timeline.t6.title: ECFA signed during his presidency
strings.timeline.t6.text: The heads of the SEF and ARATS signed ECFA in Chongqing; it entered into force on 12 September. Authorized institutional representatives signed it, not Ma personally. Early-harvest tariff measures had a separate implementation timetable.
strings.timeline.t7.title: First presidential inauguration
strings.timeline.t7.text: After winning the 22 March election, he succeeded Chen Shui-bian, returning the KMT to government. The presidency and KMT chairmanship are separate offices and do not share one identical continuous tenure.
strings.timeline.t8.title: Takes office as Taipei mayor
strings.timeline.t8.text: He succeeded Chen Shui-bian after winning the mayoral election and won again in 2002. The city roster records the last day of his second term as 24 December 2006, with Hau Lung-bin taking office the following day.
